remedy_summary: No SAMR decision before deadline; deal terminated. SAMR said (27 Jul) remedies offered were insufficient. Trade-war timing debated.
Approval announced by Marvell 28 Jun 2018; no conditions mentioned in results (unconditional is an inference); closed 6 Jul 2018.
Marvell announced SAMR approval 23 Mar 2021 ahead of its own H2-2021 guidance; no conditions mentioned (inference).

Re-filed/accepted 12 Feb 2020, approved in Phase 2: no bundling/tying, continued supply on FRAND terms, interoperability, open-source commitment; 6 years. SAMR opened a probe on Nvidia in Dec 2024 tied to these conditions.

AMD commitment plan 13 Jan 2022; no discrimination on price/delivery/service, no bundling, keep Xilinx flexibility/ARM compatibility, interoperability, continue supply to China and support local partners; 6 years.
No tying of Fibre Channel/Ethernet adapters to VMware software, keep VMware interoperable with third-party hardware in China, protect third-party confidential information; reportedly 10 years.
II-VI announced SAMR antitrust clearance 28 Jun 2022 after repeated delays; no conditions described (unconditional is an inference).
Companies announced SAMR clearance 29 Jul 2022; closed about 3 Aug 2022; HSR expired 21 Jan 2022; no conditions described (inference). Announcement date approximate.

MaxLinear terminated 26 Jul 2023; Silicon Motion calls termination invalid and is arbitrating in Singapore (SIAC). The search reported SAMR approval about 10 hours before termination per Silicon Motion; not independently verified, so SAMR outcome not coded.
No timely SAMR confirmation; termination notice effective 19 Mar 2021 announced 29 Mar 2021; Applied paid $154M fee. Announcement date from memory.
SAMR never approved by extended outside date 15 Aug 2023; $353M fee to Tower. US and EU approvals already obtained. Announcement date from memory.
SAMR approval not received by outside date; DuPont terminated and paid $162.5M; analysts split on whether it was SAMR or DuPont's choice.

Eight conditions: honour existing contracts, maintain and renew interoperability agreements, no bundling or tying, divest optical/photonic simulation and power-analysis units; behavioral parts 10 years. Decision followed US EDA export-control easing.
